undergraduate_aid_policy.policy_summary: MIT is need-blind for undergraduate applicants worldwide and meets 100% of demonstrated financial need without loans. For families with typical assets, MIT states that income below $200,000 qualifies for full tuition coverage and income below $100,000 for a $0 expected parent contribution. A $0 parent contribution does not mean that students have no costs or responsibilities.

doctorate_funding_guarantee.notes: MIT graduate funding varies significantly by program. Some programs provide full tuition funding and a stipend; applicants should use the individual program's terms and offer letter for amount, duration, and coverage.

scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: Current catalogued Imperial Business School MSc Finance, MSc Financial Technology, and Full-Time MBA cards; the 2027-28 award page covers eligible Master’s programmes including Full-Time MBA.
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: Home and Overseas applicants entering an eligible Imperial Business School MSc or MBA programme
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: New entrants with outstanding leadership potential, strong all-round applications and a demonstrated or prospective impact in business or society; confirm the eligible course.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: The listed MSc and Full-Time MBA programmes are one-year courses; check the award offer for payment conditions.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: Competitive selection; the official scholarship page does not state a course-level award count.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: Follow the selected course’s 2027 admission rounds; the award is considered with the corresponding admissions-round decision.
scholarships_and_funding.award_deadline_note: No separate fixed date is published; invited MSc written or MBA video assessment follows the course application.
steps: Submit the eligible Imperial Business School MSc or MBA application.
After invitation, submit the scholarship assessment: written for MSc or video for MBA.
documents: Eligible course application and its required documents
Invited written assessment for MSc or video assessment for MBA
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: MSc: GBP 25,000; Full-Time MBA: up to 50% of tuition fees. An award is not guaranteed.
scholarships_and_funding.description: For new entrants across specified Imperial Business School master’s programmes. The 2027-28 award is £25,000 for MSc programmes and up to 50% of tuition fees for MBA programmes.

scholarships_and_funding.name: Imperial Bursary (Home Fee Status Only)
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: For 2026-27, the standard annual award is GBP 5,000 for household income GBP 0–16,000; GBP 4,400 for GBP 16,001–50,000; GBP 3,300 for GBP 50,001–55,000; GBP 2,200 for GBP 55,001–60,000; or GBP 1,000 for GBP 60,001–70,000. Home MBBS students receive additional bursary in London clinical years 5 and 6; eligible care leavers and estranged students may receive an additional GBP 500.
scholarships_and_funding.description: For Home undergraduate students starting in autumn 2026 or 2027 with household income below £70,000; award is £1,000–£5,000 per year by income. Eligible students qualify automatically.
scholarships_and_funding.academic_year: Autumn 2026 and 2027 course starts
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: Catalogued Imperial undergraduate courses, including integrated undergraduate degrees; Home fee status only.
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: Imperial undergraduate students assessed for Home fee status, with annual household income below GBP 70,000, who apply for a means-tested government loan.
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: Applicants must be Imperial undergraduates with Home fee status, household income below GBP 70,000, and an application for a means-tested government loan through their regional funding body. Imperial assesses Home status after application; nationality alone does not establish it. Overseas-fee students and postgraduate students are ineligible.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Assessed each academic year based on continued undergraduate attendance, Home fee status, household income and required government-loan assessment.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: No competitive selection is published; eligible students qualify automatically after the income and fee-status criteria are met.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: No separate bursary application; complete the regional means-tested government-loan application for the course year.
scholarships_and_funding.award_application_deadline: Imperial must receive household income information by 31 May after the academic year starts; for autumn 2027 entrants, 31 May 2028.
scholarships_and_funding.deadline_timezone: Not specified by Imperial
steps: Apply for a means-tested government loan through the relevant regional funding body, even if you do not intend to borrow it.
Consent to sharing the household-income information with Imperial for bursary assessment.
No separate Imperial Bursary application is required; Imperial confirms the amount after the student-finance assessment.
documents: Household-income information submitted through the regional student-finance process

scholarships_and_funding.name: Imperial Inspires Scholarship
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: All catalogued full-time Imperial undergraduate courses, including integrated MEng and MSci degrees. Imperial also offers Inspires for selected full-time postgraduate taught courses, but the 2027 participating PGT course list is not published; no PGT card is linked here.
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: New international applicants who are assessed for the Overseas tuition fee rate and meet the eligible course requirements; fee status is assessed by Imperial, not inferred from nationality alone.
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: For 2027 entry, applicants must be new full-time undergraduate entrants assessed for the Overseas tuition rate, meet the chosen course’s entry requirements, and apply to an eligible Imperial undergraduate course. The FAQs confirm all undergraduate courses, including MEng and MSci, participate; selected PGT eligibility is course-specific and the 2027 list is not yet published.
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: At least GBP 15,000 per year for each year of the course, towards tuition fees and living costs. The award is partial; the offer letter states how it is split.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Award continues for the course duration subject to satisfactory academic progression and continuing eligibility; awards longer than 11 months are reviewed annually. It is not paid during interruption or repeat years.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: At least 300 full-time Overseas-fee scholarships across four faculties for 2027 entry; competitive and discretionary, not guaranteed.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: The UCAS application deadline varies by course (Medicine has an earlier deadline); the scholarship requires an invitation after the course application.
scholarships_and_funding.award_deadline_note: There is no separate fixed applicant deadline before invitation; undergraduate award decisions are scheduled by mid-April 2027.
scholarships_and_funding.deadline_timezone: UK time for course deadlines; award decisions follow Imperial’s published admissions timetable.
steps: Submit the undergraduate UCAS course application after the 2027 cycle opens.
If eligible for a participating course, complete the separate scholarship essay invitation through the admissions i360 portal.
Undergraduate scholarship decisions are scheduled by mid-April 2027.
documents: Undergraduate UCAS application and course-specific required materials
Invited Imperial Inspires scholarship essay in the admissions i360 portal

programs.application_deadline: 2026-12-01 23:59 US Pacific Time
programs.entry_requirements: A first law degree (JD or equivalent) is required. Except under unusual circumstances, candidates ordinarily need at least two years of professional legal experience before commencing the LLM; applicants may request a waiver and explain the circumstances. Stanford Law School requires valid TOEFL scores submitted through LSAC; tests taken before January 21, 2026 require TOEFL iBT 100, while tests taken after that date require overall 5.5, with at least 5.5 in Reading and Listening and 5.0 in Writing and Speaking. finance.costs_breakdown_note: Official 2026-27 undergraduate standard student budget for Autumn, Winter, and Spring: tuition USD 67,731; housing/food and other living figures are estimates/allowances, not a program price or net price. New students pay one-time orientation USD 525 and document fee USD 250. Cardinal Care is separately charged unless eligible comparable coverage is approved; international students are budgeted for this insurance.

financial_aid.merit_based_note: Undergraduate financial aid is 100% need-based. Stanford does not award academic or athletic merit scholarships for general undergraduate admission. (NCAA Division I athletic grants-in-aid are awarded independently).
financial_aid.need_policy_international_note: CRITICAL: Stanford is NEED-AWARE for international undergraduate applicants. Financial need is factored into the admissions decision. International applicants must apply for financial aid concurrently with their application; students who do not apply for aid upon admission are ineligible to receive institutional aid in subsequent years.
financial_aid.no_loans_note: Standard financial aid packages contain Stanford scholarships, federal/state grants, and work-study. No student loans are required.

under_100k.benefit: For families with typical assets and income below $100,000, Stanford expects no parent contribution toward educational costs. Students remain responsible for their own contribution from savings and employment.

under_150k.benefit: For families with typical assets and income below $150,000, Stanford states that the expected parent contribution is low enough for need-based aid and grants to cover tuition for students living on campus.

above_150k.benefit: Need-based scholarship aid scaled to family size, number of children in college, and demonstrated financial circumstances.

application_forms: FAFSA (US Citizens and Eligible Non-Citizens; School Code: 001305)
International Student Application for Financial Assistance (ISAFA) for eligible international students
financial_aid.income_thresholds_note: These income guidelines assume typical assets and US cost-of-living assumptions; Stanford says they may not apply to families living outside the United States.

phd_funding_guarantee.commitment: Stanford provides continuous 12-month funding to all enrolled PhD and DMA students in good academic standing for up to the first five years. The funding combination is tailored to the degree program.
components: Funding is provided through a combination of external fellowships, Stanford fellowships, research assistantships, and teaching assistantships; programs tailor the combination.
The commitment is funded at Stanford’s 20-hour-per-week Research Assistantship minimum; degree programs and faculty advisors arrange the support.
The university-wide policy does not prescribe one tuition unit load or a universal Cardinal Care subsidy; exact tuition and insurance treatment depends on the program and funding source.

scholarships_and_funding.name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: All full-time Stanford graduate degree programs, including the LLM, subject to current cohort eligibility and stated exceptions. KHS is a separate competitive award; it is not Stanford Law School funding.
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: Applicants from all countries; first bachelor’s degree earned January 2020 or later (military service exception); must separately apply to and enroll in an eligible Stanford graduate degree
scholarships_and_funding.academic_year: 2027 cohort
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: For the 2027 cohort, applicants must apply to KHS and be admitted to and enroll in a full-time Stanford graduate degree starting in the same year, and meet the first-bachelor’s-date rule (January 2020 or later, with the military exception). KHS says there are no restrictions by field of study and lists eligible degrees including JD, MA, MBA, MD, MS, and PhD; its explicit exclusions do not include LLM. Selection is highly competitive and not guaranteed. For Stanford MBA applicants to the 2027 cohort, KHS eligibility requires submitting the MBA application by GSB Round 1 (2026-09-09); that date has passed as of 2026-09-24. Applicants who submitted by the deadline may continue their KHS application before the October 6 KHS deadline; this does not disqualify timely submitters.
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: Up to three years of tuition and associated fees, living and academic expenses, and annual travel stipend for selected KHS Scholars, subject to program eligibility and actual degree duration; not an automatic award or a net-price estimate.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Up to three years; not a general renewable award beyond the scholar’s eligible degree period.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: Highly selective; KHS publishes no formula or guaranteed qualifying score.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: Stanford graduate program deadline; varies by program and may be earlier than 2026-12-01
scholarships_and_funding.deadline_timezone: US Pacific Time
steps: Check the 2027 cohort eligibility rules.
Submit the KHS application by October 6, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Pacific Time.
Submit a separate Stanford graduate degree application by the earlier of the program deadline for KHS applicants or December 1, 2026.
For Stanford MBA applicants, submit the MBA application by GSB Round 1 (2026-09-09) to meet KHS eligibility; timely applicants may submit their KHS application by October 6, 2026.

name: Harvard University
description: Harvard University is a private Ivy League research university in Cambridge and Boston, Massachusetts. Founded in 1636, it is the oldest institution of higher learning in the United States and among the most prestigious in the world. Harvard encompasses Harvard College for undergraduate education and 12 degree-granting graduate and professional schools, including Harvard Business School, Harvard Law School, Harvard Medical School, Harvard Kennedy School, and the Kenneth C. Griffin Graduate School of Arts and Sciences.

requirements.summary: HGSE Ed.M. admission uses the online application, statement of purpose, short essay, résumé, three recommendations, transcripts, and English evidence when required. GRE is optional. Deadline for 2027-28 is January 5, 2027.
application_materials: USD 85 application fee or approved waiver

programs.funding_note: HGSE need-based grant and Saul Zaentz fellowship applications for 2027-28 are due February 12, 2027. Saul Zaentz is limited to early-childhood education candidates and is not universal Ed.M. aid.

programs.name: Computer Science (PhD)
programs.school: Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences / Harvard Griffin GSAS
programs.requirements_note: Program-specific requirements vary; check the official department page.

requirements.summary: Apply through Harvard Griffin GSAS, selecting Engineering and Applied Sciences and PhD Computer Science. GRE General and GRE Mathematics or Physics Subject Tests are optional for 2027-2028 entry. The program page does not specify a department writing sample or personal-statement requirement; follow the current GSAS application checklist.
requirements.application_materials: GSAS online application; academic transcripts; three recommendation letters; statement of purpose; English proficiency evidence when required; GRE General and GRE Mathematics or Physics Subject Tests are optional.

programs.tuition_note: GSAS PhD gross tuition schedule: USD 59,048 for years 1-2, USD 15,352 for years 3-4, and USD 3,906 continuation fee thereafter. Health fees and other costs are additional; support in an individual offer may cover costs. This is not net price and not a 2027-28 rate.
programs.funding_note: GSAS PhD financial support terms are program- and student-specific and are stated in the individual Notice of Financial Support; do not assume a universal amount or duration.

programs.name: Economics (PhD)
programs.requirements_note: Program-specific requirements vary; check the official department page.

requirements.summary: Applicants should have economics coursework beyond introductory principles and demonstrate research ability. Calculus and linear algebra are minimum mathematical preparation; real analysis is common among successful applicants but is not required. A writing sample is required and may be single- or co-authored; GRE General is required. The program does not accept a personal statement.
requirements.application_materials: GSAS online application; academic transcripts; three recommendation letters; statement of purpose; required GRE General; required writing sample (single- or co-authored); English proficiency evidence when required.

programs.tuition_note: GSAS PhD gross tuition schedule: USD 59,048 for years 1-2, USD 15,352 for years 3-4, and USD 3,906 continuation fee thereafter. Health fees and other costs are additional; support in an individual offer may cover costs. This is not net price and not a 2027-28 rate.
programs.funding_note: GSAS PhD financial support terms are program- and student-specific and are stated in the individual Notice of Financial Support; do not assume a universal amount or duration.

programs.name: Biological and Biomedical Sciences (PhD)
programs.school: Harvard Griffin GSAS / Harvard Integrated Life Sciences / Harvard Medical School
programs.requirements_note: GRE tests are not accepted; confirm BBS international English thresholds and current requirements on its official page.

requirements.summary: BBS applicants submit a research-focused statement of purpose and a personal statement; the application includes interviews by invitation. GRE General and GRE Subject Tests are not accepted. English test minimums apply when required: TOEFL iBT 5 overall and 4.5 Speaking (100/23 for tests before Jan 21, 2026), or IELTS 7 overall and 6.5 Speaking.
requirements.application_materials: GSAS online application; academic transcripts; three recommendation letters; research-focused statement of purpose; required personal statement; English proficiency evidence when required; GRE scores are not accepted; interviews by invitation.

programs.tuition_note: GSAS PhD gross tuition schedule: USD 59,048 for years 1-2, USD 15,352 for years 3-4, and USD 3,906 continuation fee thereafter. Health fees and other costs are additional; support in an individual offer may cover costs. This is not net price and not a 2027-28 rate.
programs.funding_note: GSAS PhD financial support terms are program- and student-specific and are stated in the individual Notice of Financial Support; do not assume a universal amount or duration.

programs.name: Physics (PhD)
programs.requirements_note: GRE General and GRE Physics Subject Test are required; list the six most advanced courses (four physics, two mathematics).

requirements.summary: Applicants should have strong undergraduate physics and mathematics preparation. In the application, list six advanced courses (four physics and two mathematics). GRE General is optional; the Physics GRE Subject Test is required.
requirements.application_materials: GSAS online application; academic transcripts; three recommendation letters; statement of purpose; six advanced undergraduate courses (four physics and two mathematics) listed in the application; required GRE Physics Subject Test; GRE General optional; English proficiency evidence when required.

programs.tuition_note: GSAS PhD gross tuition schedule: USD 59,048 for years 1-2, USD 15,352 for years 3-4, and USD 3,906 continuation fee thereafter. Health fees and other costs are additional; support in an individual offer may cover costs. This is not net price and not a 2027-28 rate.
programs.funding_note: GSAS PhD financial support terms are program- and student-specific and are stated in the individual Notice of Financial Support; do not assume a universal amount or duration.

programs.name: Government (PhD)
programs.requirements_note: GRE General is required; submit a recent scholarly or critical writing sample. A coordinated JD/PhD requires a separate HLS application.

requirements.summary: Government PhD applicants must submit a recent scholarly or critical writing sample of any length, a personal statement, and GRE General scores. Current published English minimums are TOEFL iBT 5 overall and 4.5 Speaking (105/23 for tests before Jan 21, 2026), or IELTS 7.5 overall and 6.5 Speaking. Coordinated JD/PhD applicants submit separate applications to GSAS and HLS.
requirements.application_materials: GSAS online application; academic transcripts; three recommendation letters; statement of purpose; required personal statement; required recent scholarly or critical writing sample (any length); required GRE General; English proficiency evidence when required; separate HLS application for coordinated JD/PhD applicants.

programs.tuition_note: GSAS PhD gross tuition schedule: USD 59,048 for years 1-2, USD 15,352 for years 3-4, and USD 3,906 continuation fee thereafter. Health fees and other costs are additional; support in an individual offer may cover costs. This is not net price and not a 2027-28 rate.
programs.funding_note: GSAS PhD financial support terms are program- and student-specific and are stated in the individual Notice of Financial Support; do not assume a universal amount or duration.

programs.name: Architecture (MArch I)
programs.tuition_note: Published 2026-27 annual tuition only; mandatory and living costs are additional. 2027-28 rates are not published.
programs.requirements_note: GSD currently lists the prospective financial-aid deadline only as mid-April, without a year-specific timestamp. Confirm the cycle date in the official aid application.

requirements.summary: MArch I is Harvard GSD’s first professional architecture degree. Applicants need a bachelor’s degree and must meet the program’s academic and portfolio requirements; the 2027-2028 application is due January 5, 2027 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
application_materials: Architecture portfolio using the MArch I specifications
USD 90 application fee or approved waiver

programs.name: Architecture (MArch II)
programs.tuition_note: Published 2026-27 annual tuition only; mandatory and living costs are additional. 2027-28 rates are not published.
programs.requirements_note: GSD currently lists the prospective financial-aid deadline only as mid-April, without a year-specific timestamp. Confirm the cycle date in the official aid application.

requirements.summary: MArch II is a post-professional architecture degree for applicants with a qualifying completed or in-progress five-year professional architecture degree. It is not NAAB-accredited and does not satisfy the education requirement for NCARB licensure. The 2027-2028 application is due January 5, 2027 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
application_materials: Architecture portfolio using the MArch II specifications
USD 90 application fee or approved waiver

programs.name: Public Health (MPH-45, residential)
programs.school: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
programs.requirements_note: The exact 2027-28 deadline for MPH-45 residential is not confirmed in the reviewed official source. Select this format in SOPHAS and verify its deadline, prerequisites and documents on the official program page.
programs.tuition_note: 2026-27 annual tuition for MPH-45 residential: USD 77,400. Mandatory health insurance and health fee apply to residential MPH-45/65; they are not assessed for online MPH-Generalist. This is not the 2027-28 price.
programs.funding_note: Eligible MPH-45, MPH-65 and MPH-Generalist applicants, including international applicants, may apply for Chan grants/scholarships. Funding is limited and the 2027-28 aid deadline is unconfirmed; check the current Chan aid application.

requirements.summary: MPH-45 is a one-year residential 45-credit professional degree. Applicants generally need a bachelor’s degree plus five or more years of relevant health experience, a health-related master’s plus at least two years of relevant experience, a prior doctoral degree, or completion of the primary clinical year in medical/dental school. Individual MPH fields can add eligibility conditions; check the selected field page. Apply through SOPHAS.
application_materials: Program-specific statement of purpose and objectives (up to 600 words for MPH)

application_deadlines.cycle: 2027-2028 entry; school says December 1 for most programs but selected MPH field not fixed

programs.funding_note: Eligible MPH-45, MPH-65 and MPH-Generalist applicants, including international applicants, may apply for Chan grants/scholarships. Funding is limited and the 2027-28 aid deadline is unconfirmed; check the current Chan aid application.

requirements.summary: MPH-65 is a 1.5-year residential 65-credit degree for applicants with a bachelor’s degree and at least two years of contiguous full-time work experience in a relevant area. Individual MPH fields can add requirements. Apply through SOPHAS.
application_materials: Program-specific statement of purpose and objectives (up to 600 words for MPH)

application_deadlines.cycle: 2027-2028 entry; school says December 1 for most programs but selected MPH field not fixed

programs.school: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
programs.requirements_note: The exact 2027-28 deadline for MPH-Generalist online/part-time is not confirmed in the reviewed official source. Select this format in SOPHAS and verify its deadline, prerequisites and documents on the official program page.

programs.funding_note: Eligible MPH-45, MPH-65 and MPH-Generalist applicants, including international applicants, may apply for Chan grants/scholarships. Funding is limited and the 2027-28 aid deadline is unconfirmed; check the current Chan aid application.

requirements.summary: MPH-Generalist is a 45-credit online, part-time program completed over two years. Applicants generally need a bachelor’s degree plus five or more years of relevant health experience, a health-related master’s degree, or a prior doctoral degree; current medical and dental students are ineligible. Students in this fully online program are not eligible for a Harvard-sponsored student visa. Apply through SOPHAS.
application_materials: Program-specific statement of purpose and objectives (up to 600 words for MPH)

admission_categories.label: Harvard College (Undergraduate First-Year)
admission_categories.description: Harvard College first-year admission is one shared route for the listed concentrations; students are not admitted by concentration. Fall 2027 entry offers Restrictive Early Action and Regular Decision.
admission_categories.fee_waiver_policy: Need-based application fee waiver available on request via Common App, Coalition, or direct school counselor certification without prejudice.

admission_rounds.name: Restrictive Early Action (REA)
admission_rounds.description: Non-binding early round. Applicants may not apply to early programs at other private US universities or binding programs at public institutions.

admission_rounds.name: Regular Decision (RD)
admission_rounds.description: Standard decision round allowing applicants to compare financial aid and admission offers until May 1.

admission_categories.testing_policy: SAT or ACT scores are required for applicants entering Fall 2025 and later. Harvard permits alternative examination results only in exceptional cases when applicants cannot access SAT or ACT testing.
extra_requirements: Common Application or Coalition Application by Scoir; QuestBridge applicants follow the applicable QuestBridge route
Harvard College questions and personal essay
School report and transcript with counselor recommendation
Two teacher recommendations
Midyear School Report and final report if admitted
SAT or ACT (or stated exceptional-case alternatives when testing is inaccessible)
USD 95 application fee or approved fee waiver

scholarships.name: Harvard Financial Aid Initiative (HFAI)
scholarships.eligibility: All admitted undergraduate students (domestic and international)
scholarships.coverage: For families with typical assets and income of $100,000 or less, Harvard describes attendance as free; aid covers billed expenses and includes a $2,000 first-year Start-Up Grant. Families with income up to $200,000 receive at least full tuition coverage, with additional aid based on individual circumstances. Harvard meets 100% of demonstrated need without student loans.

requirement_profiles.label: SAT
requirement_profiles.description: Harvard College first-year undergraduate route for applicants submitting SAT scores.

score_profile.source_note: Derived from official Harvard CDS 2023-2024 SAT section percentiles (EBRW 740/760/780 and Math 760/790/800), summed to composite equivalents 1500/1550/1580.

funding_options.label: Harvard College - Standard Family Contribution
funding_options.description: Standard Harvard College cost of attendance based on family financial contribution assessment.

funding_options.label: Harvard College - Harvard Financial Aid Initiative (HFAI Grant)
funding_options.description: Need-blind admission with 100% of demonstrated need met without loans. For families with typical assets and income of $100,000 or less, Harvard describes attendance as free and includes a $2,000 first-year Start-Up Grant. Families with income up to $200,000 receive at least full tuition coverage; additional aid depends on individual circumstances.

requirement_profiles.requirements_note: Harvard publishes no minimum SAT, ACT, or GPA score; test scores are reviewed in the context of the full application.

requirement_profiles.label: ACT
requirement_profiles.description: Harvard College first-year undergraduate route for applicants submitting ACT scores.

score_profile.source_note: Derived from official Harvard Common Data Set reports ACT Composite 25th percentile of 34 and 75th percentile of 36 for enrolled first-year students.

funding_options.label: Harvard College - ACT
funding_options.description: Standard Harvard College route for applicants submitting ACT scores.

funding_options.label: Harvard College - Financial Aid (Grant)
funding_options.description: Need-blind admission with 100% of demonstrated need met without loans. For families with typical assets and income of $100,000 or less, Harvard describes attendance as free and includes a $2,000 first-year Start-Up Grant. Families with income up to $200,000 receive at least full tuition coverage; additional aid depends on individual circumstances.

requirement_profiles.requirements_note: Harvard publishes no minimum SAT, ACT, or GPA score; test scores are reviewed in the context of the full application.

admission_categories.cycle_note: The source lists recurring Restrictive Early Action and Regular Decision dates without an entry year.
admission_categories.program_scope_note: One first-year Harvard College admission route for all listed concentrations; applicants are not admitted by concentration.

admission_categories.label: Harvard Griffin GSAS (Doctorate / PhD Programs)
admission_categories.description: Harvard Griffin GSAS doctoral programs in 57 disciplines. PhD financial support is specified in each admitted student’s Notice of Financial Support and varies by program; continued support requires full-time enrollment, satisfactory academic progress, and annual renewal or activation.
admission_categories.fee_waiver_policy: Application fee waivers available for demonstrated financial hardship and participants in recognized academic pipeline/diversity programs.

admission_rounds.name: Program-Specific Admissions Deadline
admission_rounds.deadline: Varies by degree program; check the relevant program page.
admission_rounds.notification: Program-specific; check the relevant program page.
admission_rounds.reply_deadline: Program-specific; see the offer and program instructions.
admission_rounds.description: Harvard Griffin GSAS deadlines vary by program. The current general admissions page does not publish one shared doctoral deadline or decision date.

funding_options.label: GSAS 5-Year Guaranteed Funding Package
funding_options.description: Program-specific PhD financial support may include tuition grants, health insurance fees, and living support. The individual Notice of Financial Support sets the package and conditions; support varies by program.

scholarships.name: GSAS 5-Year Guaranteed Doctoral Support Package
scholarships.eligibility: Admitted Harvard Griffin GSAS PhD students; continued eligibility requires full-time enrollment and satisfactory academic progress, as stated in the individual Notice of Financial Support.
scholarships.coverage: Program-specific support may combine tuition grants, health insurance fees, stipends, teaching fellowships, research assistantships, and other academic appointments. The individual offer defines the covered years and amounts.
scholarships.renewal: Continuing students must renew or activate support annually; eligibility depends on full-time enrollment and satisfactory academic progress.

requirement_profiles.label: GSAS PhD Admission Profile
requirement_profiles.description: Program-specific doctoral admission requirements, supporting documents, and deadlines; consult the selected degree program.

funding_options.label: GSAS 5-Year Guaranteed Funding Package
funding_options.description: Guaranteed financial support for 5 years: 100% tuition, health insurance, and $45,000 - $51,500 annual living stipend.

requirement_profiles.requirements_note: Harvard Griffin GSAS does not publish a university-wide GPA cutoff. Requirements vary by degree program.

admission_categories.program_scope_note: One GSAS portal, but each department sets its own deadline, tests, and document rules.

admission_categories.label: Harvard Business School (HBS - MBA)
admission_categories.description: Two-year full-time Master in Business Administration (MBA) on the Boston campus. HBS offers need-based scholarships; its current published figures report that about half of MBA students receive a scholarship and 10% receive full tuition.
admission_categories.fee_waiver_policy: Need-based application fee waiver available for active-duty military, veterans, and applicants demonstrating extreme financial need.

admission_rounds.name: Round 1
admission_rounds.reply_deadline: See the admission offer; HBS does not publish a reply date on the application dates page.
admission_rounds.description: For the MBA Class of 2029, matriculating Fall 2027.

admission_rounds.name: Round 2
admission_rounds.reply_deadline: See the admission offer; HBS does not publish a reply date on the application dates page.
admission_rounds.description: For the MBA Class of 2029, matriculating Fall 2027.

funding_options.label: HBS Need-Based Fellowship
funding_options.description: Need-based scholarships are available to admitted MBA students. HBS reports about 50% of students receive a need-based scholarship and 10% receive full-tuition scholarships; award amounts depend on individual circumstances.

funding_options.label: HBS Standard Self-Funded
funding_options.description: Published MBA tuition is $84,760 for academic year 2026-27; this is tuition, not total cost of attendance. See the official cost table for fees and living costs.

scholarships.name: HBS Need-Based Fellowship
scholarships.eligibility: All admitted MBA candidates demonstrating financial need (domestic and international)
scholarships.coverage: Need-based gift aid; HBS reports an average scholarship of about $100,000 over two years and full-tuition scholarships for 10% of students. Individual awards vary and these published statistics are not a guaranteed award.
scholarships.competition: HBS reports approximately 50% of MBA students receive need-based scholarships; the individual award is need-based and not guaranteed.

requirement_profiles.label: HBS MBA Profile
requirement_profiles.description: For the regular MBA Class of 2029 (Fall 2027): HBS requires a college/university degree; the international-applicant guidance specifies a degree equivalent to a four-year U.S. bachelor’s degree and recognizes equivalent international three-year bachelor’s degrees. Full-time work experience is strongly recommended but is not a formal prerequisite. No minimum GPA or GMAT/GRE score is published.

funding_options.label: HBS Need-Based Fellowship
funding_options.description: 100% need-based tuition assistance; roughly 50% receive awards averaging ~$46,000/year.

requirement_profiles.requirements_note: The regular MBA application has two deadlines in this cycle. Do not apply the 2+2 deferred-admission deadline to this profile. HBS publishes no minimum GPA or GMAT/GRE score.
requirement_profiles.eligibility: College or university degree required. HBS says international applicants need a degree equivalent to a four-year U.S. bachelor’s; equivalent international three-year bachelor’s degrees may qualify. HBS strongly recommends at least two years of full-time professional work experience by enrollment but does not state it as a formal eligibility requirement.
application_materials: Online HBS application and acceptance of application policies
GMAT or GRE score; official score report requested, due by the application deadline
English-language test score when required by HBS international-applicant policy; no minimum score is stated, but HBS discourages scores below its published levels
Two online recommendations (HBS prefers one current or former supervisor)
Application fee or approved fee waiver
requirement_profiles.interview_and_post_interview: Interview is by invitation and required if invited. Applicants invited to interview must submit an online post-interview reflection within 24 hours.

extra_requirements: Online HBS application and acceptance of application policies
Academic transcripts from post-secondary institutions
GMAT or GRE score; official score report requested, due by the application deadline
English-language test score when required by HBS international-applicant policy; no minimum score is stated, but HBS discourages scores below its published levels
Application essays
Two online recommendations (HBS prefers one current or former supervisor)
Professional resume
Application fee or approved fee waiver

admission_categories.label: Harvard Law School (HLS - Juris Doctor)
admission_categories.description: Three-year Juris Doctor (JD) professional degree at Harvard Law School, with Regular Decision for Fall 2027 entry.
admission_categories.fee_waiver_policy: Fee waiver granted to applicants with an approved LSAC fee waiver or demonstrated extreme need.

admission_rounds.name: Regular Decision
admission_rounds.notification: Starting no sooner than January 2027; target is by early April 2027.
admission_rounds.description: Primary admissions round for entering first-year JD students.

funding_options.label: HLS Need-Based Grant
funding_options.description: Need-based J.D. grant capped at tuition; some applicants receive loans only. LIPP is a separate post-graduation process and is not part of this grant or a current-cost offset.

funding_options.label: HLS Standard Tuition
funding_options.description: Published JD tuition is $84,400 for academic year 2026-27; this is tuition, not total cost of attendance. See the official cost table for fees and living costs.

scholarships.name: HLS Grant & Low Income Protection Plan (LIPP)
scholarships.eligibility: JD students may apply for annual need-based aid. HLS grant eligibility depends on the annual need calculation; LIPP has separate loan, employment, and income rules for eligible graduates.
scholarships.coverage: HLS need-based grants are capped at tuition; some aid applicants receive loans only. LIPP provides loan-repayment assistance under its current program rules, which vary by eligible debt and employment plan.
scholarships.competition: HLS reports that approximately 50% of JD financial-aid applicants qualify for HLS grant assistance; others may qualify for loans.
scholarships.renewal: Need-based aid is reassessed each academic year. LIPP participation requires a separate application and approval under the current program rules.

requirement_profiles.label: HLS JD Profile
requirement_profiles.description: Fall 2027 J.D. is a three-year, full-time professional law degree. Applicants must hold or expect to hold a bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent) before August 2027, subject to HLS’s stated degree-conferral exception. Required materials: LSAC application and CAS report; LSAT or GRE taken by February 1, 2027; all undergraduate and graduate transcripts; two recommendation letters (up to three); one- to two-page resume; both required written statements; and the $90 fee or approved waiver. The application deadline is February 5, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. ET.

funding_options.label: HLS Need-Based Grant
funding_options.description: Need-based J.D. grant capped at tuition; some applicants receive loans only. LIPP is a separate post-graduation process and is not part of this grant or a current-cost offset.

requirement_profiles.eligibility: Must hold or expect to hold a bachelor’s degree or international equivalent before August 2027, except where all degree requirements are completed before September and the degree is conferred after September.
application_materials: All undergraduate and graduate transcripts sent to LSAC/CAS; foreign postsecondary transcripts are subject to HLS’s stated evaluation rule and exception
LSAT or GRE General Test taken no later than February 1, 2027; HLS does not consider GRE when a valid LSAT score is on file
Two letters of recommendation required; up to three accepted through LSAC; at least one academic recommender is strongly recommended
Statement of Purpose and Statement of Perspective, each one to two pages and double-spaced
Character and Fitness Questions; optional brief addendum if relevant
$90 application fee or approved fee waiver
requirement_profiles.decision_window: Starting no sooner than January 2027; HLS aims to notify all applicants by early April 2027.
requirement_profiles.interview_policy: Interview may be offered by invitation; the admissions office contacts selected applicants.
requirement_profiles.requirements_note: The LSAT/GRE must be taken by February 1, five days before the application deadline. Two letters are required; a third is optional. Both written statements are required.

extra_requirements: Online application submitted through LSAC
LSAC Credential Assembly Service (CAS) report
All undergraduate and graduate transcripts sent to LSAC/CAS; foreign postsecondary transcripts are subject to HLS’s stated evaluation rule and exception
LSAT or GRE General Test taken no later than February 1, 2027; HLS does not consider GRE when a valid LSAT score is on file
Two letters of recommendation required; up to three accepted through LSAC; at least one academic recommender is strongly recommended
Required one- to two-page resume
Statement of Purpose and Statement of Perspective, each one to two pages and double-spaced
Character and Fitness Questions; optional brief addendum if relevant
$90 application fee or approved fee waiver

admission_categories.label: Harvard Kennedy School MPP and two-year MPA
admission_categories.description: Shared 2027-2028 application route for the Master in Public Policy (MPP) and the two-year Master in Public Administration (MPA) only. The one-year MC/MPA and MPA in International Development are separate degrees and are not represented here.
admission_categories.fee_waiver_policy: Fee waivers available for applicants with documented financial hardship, AmeriCorps/Peace Corps alumni, and selected public service fellows.

admission_rounds.name: Annual Master's Admissions Round
admission_rounds.description: For the 2027-2028 academic year; one admissions deadline applies to HKS master's degree programs.

funding_options.label: HKS Public Service Fellowships
funding_options.description: HKS scholarships and fellowships are limited and competitive. Awards are generally merit-based; financial need affects the amount of some awards. Most funding applies to tuition and fees; a limited number of awards include stipends. Loan repayment assistance is a separate post-graduation program.

funding_options.label: HKS Standard Tuition
funding_options.description: Tuition and fees depend on the HKS master’s program. See program-specific profiles for amounts, scope, and source. The listed profile rates are for 2026-27; 2027-28 rates had not been published as of September 23, 2026.

scholarships.name: HKS Public Leadership Fellowships & LRAP
scholarships.eligibility: HKS master’s applicants who submit the financial-aid application before the admission decision; eligibility varies by individual award, degree program, and any stated service or other criteria.
scholarships.coverage: Limited merit-based scholarships and fellowships, generally applied to tuition and fees; some awards include a living stipend. Award amount and coverage vary by program and award. Loan repayment assistance is separate and applies after graduation under its own rules.
scholarships.competition: Funding is limited and competitive; HKS states that scholarship and fellowship selection is merit-based, with financial need affecting the amount of some awards.
scholarships.application_process: Submit the HKS Financial Aid Application after applying for admission and before the admission decision.
scholarships.renewal: Award-specific; the public general funding page does not state one renewal rule for all HKS awards.

requirement_profiles.label: Master in Public Policy (MPP)
requirement_profiles.description: MPP prerequisites for 2027-2028: bachelor’s degree with a strong academic record and evidence of quantitative proficiency such as undergraduate economics, statistics, or calculus. Work experience is advantageous but not required; incoming students typically have 2–3 years. GRE or GMAT is required unless an eligible waiver was requested and approved before the waiver deadline. The application requires the program essays, résumé/CV, three recommendations, transcripts, required test scores, and $100 fee or waiver.

funding_options.label: HKS Public Service Fellowships
funding_options.description: Competitive tuition fellowships, need-based tuition waivers, and LRAP.

requirement_profiles.eligibility: Bachelor’s degree with a strong academic record; evidence of quantitative proficiency through undergraduate economics, statistics, or calculus. Work experience is not required.
application_materials: JFK essay (750 words) and Perspectives essay (250 words)
Required GRE or GMAT unless the program-specific waiver was requested and approved before the waiver deadline
English proficiency test when required by HKS policy; official valid scores must arrive by the application deadline
requirement_profiles.standardized_test_requirement: GRE or GMAT required. A waiver may apply for an overall B average or better and B+ (or equivalent) or better in statistics and/or calculus and intermediate economics; the waiver-request deadline for 2027-2028 has passed, so applicants without an earlier approved request must submit test results.
requirement_profiles.english_language_requirement: Applicants whose undergraduate degree was not conducted entirely in English must submit a single-sitting TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, or Cambridge English score. Minimums: TOEFL iBT 5 overall for tests from January 2026 onward (100 for earlier tests); IELTS 7 overall; Cambridge C1/C2 185. An English-taught undergraduate degree waives the test regardless of native language; an English-taught graduate degree alone does not.
requirement_profiles.tuition_scope: MPP tuition and mandatory fees for one academic year; not total cost of attendance

requirement_profiles.label: Master in Public Administration (MPA)

An English-taught undergraduate degree waives the test regardless of native language; an English-taught graduate degree alone does not.

scholarships_and_funding.name: Reach Oxford Scholarship
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: Oxford first-year undergraduate and integrated undergraduate courses in this catalogue, excluding Medicine.

scholarships_and_funding.academic_year: 2027 entry
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: An Oxford admission offer is required before scholarship consideration. Priority goes to applicants who have not studied at undergraduate level before and intend to return to their country after study.
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: Course fees, a grant for living costs, and one return air fare per year for 3 or 4 years depending on course. Oxford has not published a 2027-specific living-grant amount.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Continued award is subject to satisfactory academic progress; annual report required.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: Around 2–3 awards per year; competition is very high, and Oxford has no additional funding for unsuccessful candidates.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: UCAS application by 2026-10-15 18:00
scholarships_and_funding.deadline_timezone: UK time
steps: Apply for an Oxford undergraduate course through UCAS by October 15, 2026 at 6 p.m. UK time.
Receive an Oxford offer.
When the 2027 scholarship application opens in January 2027, complete the separate Reach Oxford scholarship application by January 26, 2027.
If selected, maintain satisfactory academic progress and submit the required annual report.
documents: Oxford undergraduate admission application and offer
Separate Reach Oxford scholarship application; exact form and supporting-document list for 2027 to be published in January 2027

scholarships_and_funding.name: Clarendon Fund Scholarship
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: New eligible full-time or part-time Master’s and DPhil courses in this catalogue only; all nationalities and subjects. It does not apply to undergraduate or integrated undergraduate entry.
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: Applicants of any nationality or ordinary residence who apply for a new eligible degree-bearing Master’s or DPhil course by the relevant December or January course deadline
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: Automatic consideration when the complete graduate course application is submitted by the relevant December or January funding deadline; course and scholarship selection are separate decisions.
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: Full course fees plus an annual living-cost grant for full-time study; part-time scholars receive a course-specific study-support grant. The 2027-28 numeric grant is not published; continuation charges are not covered.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Award duration follows the eligible course period, subject to award conditions; exact duration and renewal terms are determined by the course and award offer.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: Highly competitive global award; selection is based on academic excellence and potential. No award count is stated on this applicant page.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: Relevant Oxford graduate course deadline, typically December or January; exact date is course-specific
scholarships_and_funding.award_application_deadline: Same as the relevant Oxford graduate course application deadline
scholarships_and_funding.deadline_timezone: UK time; exact hour is course-specific
steps: Apply to the eligible Oxford graduate course by its relevant December or January deadline.
Submit the complete course application; there is no separate Clarendon scholarship form.
Provide the academic record, personal statement, and referees’ reports required for the course application.
documents: Complete Oxford graduate course application
Course-specific academic transcripts, statement, and referee reports; no additional Clarendon documents

scholarships_and_funding.name: Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: Oxford MSc Advanced Computer Science, MBA and BCL in this catalogue; the full official eligible-course list is broader
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: Applicants ordinarily resident in an eligible country, including Kazakhstan, for a new full-time eligible Oxford graduate course
scholarships_and_funding.academic_year: 2027-28 entry
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: Apply for a new full-time eligible course, meet the country-of-ordinary-residence rule, intend to return home, and show how the course supports public life. Deferred 2027-28 offer holders and current Oxford students are normally ineligible. A course offer by the December or January funding deadline is required.
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: 100% of course fees and a living-cost grant of at least GBP 21,805 for the agreed course fee-liability period, plus leadership development.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Covers the full fee-liability period for the agreed eligible course, subject to award terms.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: Competitive selection; eligible applicants may be interviewed online in April 2027. An eligible application and course offer do not guarantee funding.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: The chosen course’s relevant December 2026 or January 2027 funding deadline; see its official course page
scholarships_and_funding.award_application_deadline: Same course deadline: select the scholarship and upload the separate statement with the graduate application
scholarships_and_funding.deadline_timezone: UK time; exact hour depends on the course deadline
steps: Confirm that the chosen course and country of ordinary residence appear on the 2027-28 eligibility lists.
Select Weidenfeld-Hoffmann in the Oxford graduate application.
Upload the 2027-28 Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships Statement and submit by the course funding deadline.
Obtain a course offer by that deadline; attend an interview if shortlisted.
documents: Oxford graduate course application and all course-required materials
Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships Statement 2027/28
Nationality and ordinary-residence details in the graduate application

scholarships_and_funding.name: Oxford Bursary
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: Selected first undergraduate degree routes in this catalogue; not a general award for Overseas fee-status applicants. Graduate Entry Medicine A101 is outside this catalogue.
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: Eligible Home-fee-status students starting a first undergraduate degree: UK students, or Republic of Ireland nationals living in the UK or Ireland, from a lower-income household and not eligible for or not taking Crankstart; eligible EU/EEA/Swiss settled or pre-settled-status students may qualify if residence requirements are met.
scholarships_and_funding.academic_year: 2027 entry
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: No separate Oxford application. A regional student-finance agency household-income assessment is required; complete it by 30 May 2028 for 2027 starters. First undergraduate degree and Home fee-status eligibility apply.
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: Annual non-repayable living-cost bursary; 2027-28 amounts are income-banded in award_amounts. Eligible UK first-degree bursary holders may separately qualify for a distance-based Oxford Travel Supplement; that separate supplement is not included in these amounts.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Income assessment and eligibility are checked for each academic year under Oxford and government rules.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: UCAS application by 2026-10-15 18:00 UK time

scholarships_and_funding.name: Crankstart Scholarship
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: Selected first undergraduate degree routes in this catalogue; UK-residency and household-income criteria apply. Graduate Entry Medicine A101 is outside this catalogue.
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: UK residents who have been resident in the UK for at least three years other than for education, are starting their first undergraduate degree, and have annual household income of £32,500 or less.
scholarships_and_funding.academic_year: 2027 entry
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: No separate Crankstart application. Oxford makes offers based on the household-income assessment by the regional funding agency. Applicants may decline Crankstart and be assessed for an Oxford Bursary instead.
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: Annual living-cost bursary plus access to funded internships, volunteering and scholar-community activities. Separate internship and care-experienced/estranged support have additional conditions and are not guaranteed base-bursary amounts.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Annual support is assessed under the current Crankstart terms and household-income assessment.
